findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Step 2 with the Completion Scope Adjustment: annotate Step 2 to mark which listed crown-jewels are in-session (internally regenerable) vs deferred to auspicial-wily-warbler, so the two sections agree.
evidence: Step 2: 'Rotate the crown-jewels explicitly ... Gerrit admin password, opcert Ed25519 signing key, rebar-bot signing key, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys. Update every external system that trusts an old value'
Scope Adjustment: 'rotate ONLY secrets that can be regenerated internally in this session, and flag third-party or externally anchored credentials for a human/operator'
findings.finding: Step 2 instructs rotating ALL crown-jewels (Gerrit admin password, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys, etc.) and updating every external system that trusts an old value, but the Completion Scope Adjustment narrows autonomous rotation to ONLY internally-regenerable secrets and defers externally-anchored ones to follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler — the two sections send the executor in opposite directions.
scenarios: Executor follows Step 2 literally and attempts external Anthropic/Jira/Gerrit rotation the Adjustment says to defer, or vice-versa
findings.suggested_fix: Edit Step 2 to split the crown-jewel list into 'rotate now (internally regenerable)' and 'flag to auspicial-wily-warbler (externally anchored)', matching the Scope Adjustment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate each named crown-jewel as either internally-regenerable (rotate this session) or externally-anchored (flag to auspicial-wily-warbler), removing the classification ambiguity.
evidence: Scope Adjustment distinguishes 'secrets that can be regenerated internally' from 'third-party or externally anchored credentials' but no mapping of the six named secrets to those buckets is given
Signal (2) implicit acceptance criteria: the set of in-session rotations is unstated
findings.finding: The plan never enumerates WHICH of the named crown-jewels are 'internally self-regenerable' vs 'externally anchored', yet that classification is load-bearing for the narrowed close scope (which get rotated in-session vs flagged to follow-up). An executor cannot determine, without asking, whether e.g. the opcert Ed25519 signing key or SSH host keys are in-session rotations or deferred.
scenarios: Executor must decide whether SSH host keys / opcert Ed25519 key are internal-regenerable and rotate-in-session, with no stated classification
findings.suggested_fix: Add a table/list mapping each of the six secrets to internal-vs-external so the executor knows the exact in-session rotation set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the back-out/recovery procedure if a rotation fails after the Step-1 CHANGEME reset (e.g. re-seed prior value from a secure source or abort criteria) so partial-window failure is recoverable.
evidence: Step 1: 'value_wo_version goes absent -> 1 ... RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder ... user_data.sh's CHANGEME fail-fast is the safety net'
No stated back-out/restore-from-prior-value procedure if rotation does not complete in the same window
findings.finding: Step 1 resets every live seeded secret to the placeholder 'CHANGEME' before Step 2 rotates them, relying on user_data.sh fail-fast as the only safety net. The plan states no recovery/back-out for the window between the CHANGEME reset and successful rotation — if the maintenance window is interrupted or a rotation fails, affected prod services are left with a placeholder value and no described restoration path.
scenarios: Rotation of one secret fails after the CHANGEME reset; the consumer reads CHANGEME and fail-fast keeps the service down with no documented recovery
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short rollback note: capture prior values are being purged, so define the recovery as immediate re-seed of a freshly generated value and confirm ordering (rotate before restarting consumers) with a per-secret checklist to bound the failure window.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the ordering/locking contract between this apply and the concurrent 'rubied' MCP-PAT apply (e.g. serialize the two applies under the terraform state lock and run the version-scrub only AFTER both applies have committed) so neither races the shared tfstate nor leaves un-scrubbed cleartext versions.
evidence: 'Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the state scrub covers those params too'
Step 4 permanently deletes affected object versions of the shared tfstate key (~149 versions) — an irreversible destructive mutation on shared state
No lock/ordering primitive (DynamoDB state lock, apply sequencing, freeze window) is named for the two concurrent applies
findings.finding: The plan coordinates with a SEPARATE concurrent 'rubied' apply that seeds MCP-PAT params into the same remote tfstate, but does not specify an ordering or terraform state-locking mechanism to prevent the two applies from racing on the shared tfstate object — and the subsequent destructive version-scrub could purge or miss versions written by the other apply mid-flight.
scenarios: Both applies run against s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071 concurrently -> state lock contention or a lost update corrupts the tfstate
Scrub runs while rubied is still writing new SecureString versions -> a fresh cleartext MCP-PAT version is written after the scrub and survives, defeating the scrub AC
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Coordination sub-step requiring both applies to complete (verified via state pull) before the historical-version scrub begins, and confirm terraform state locking is enabled on the backend so the applies cannot run concurrently.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate /auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET (and note /auth-solutions/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET) explicitly in the apply-reset handling, Step 3 state-pull verification, and the scrub scope — it is one of the three resources migrated by the prerequisite change, is reset to CHANGEME by the same cutover apply, has no user_data.sh fail-fast, and its historical cleartext is in the same tfstate object.
evidence: Prerequisite bug eb67-b96c-dcf0-4f86 file_impact + description: 'infra/terraform/auth_sso.tf — Migrate cookie_signing_secret to value_wo/value_wo_version' (one of THREE migrated resources)

auth_sso.tf:40-46 resource aws_ssm_parameter.cookie_signing_secret name=/auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET uses value_wo=CHANGEME + value_wo_version=1 — same cutover reset semantics as /rebar/prod/ secrets

Plan Step 1: value_wo_version 'absent -> 1 for each migrated slot' resets 'each live seeded secret' — this includes cookie_signing_secret, but the safety-net claim ('user_data.sh CHANGEME fail-fast') does not apply to it since it is read by the auth-host Lambda, not by user_data.sh
versions.tf:18-20 confirms a single backend key rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate — cookie_signing_secret's historical cleartext is in the SAME object the scrub targets

Follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler DOES list /auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET and /auth-solutions/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET for external rotation, but the plan's own execution scope (apply-reset handling, state-pull verify, scrub enumeration) never names them
findings.finding: The cutover apply and state scrub omit /auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET, which is one of the three SecureString resources migrated to value_wo by the prerequisite change (auth_sso.tf:40, resource cookie_signing_secret) and is therefore reset to CHANGEME by the same value_wo_version absent->1 apply and its historical cleartext lives in the same rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate object. The plan's Step 2 rotation, Step 3 state-pull verify ('value: null for every migrated secret'), and Step 4 scrub scope all frame the affected set as '/rebar/prod/' params only and never name this /auth-solutions/-prefixed migrated secret.
findings.location: Steps 1-4 / Coordination clause; AC line 3 ('every migrated secret'); auth_sso.tf:40
scenarios: Operator applies the migration, seeds only the enumerated /rebar/prod/ crown-jewels, and leaves cookie_signing_secret at CHANGEME — the auth-host Lambda reads a placeholder HMAC key and every SSO session silently breaks (no user_data.sh fail-fast catches it)
Step 3 verification passes on /rebar/prod/ params while the reviewer never checks the /auth-solutions/ migrated secret's value in state
findings.suggested_fix: In Steps 1-3, state that the cutover reset and the value:null verification cover ALL migrated SecureString resources across both the /rebar/prod/ and /auth-solutions/ prefixes (rebar_secrets, opcert_ed25519_key, cookie_signing_secret), and note that cookie_signing_secret's CHANGEME reset must be re-seeded before the auth-host Lambda is exercised since user_data.sh's fail-fast does not guard it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Step 1's 'reset every migrated slot to CHANGEME' with the narrowed rotation scope: state explicitly how deferred (externally-anchored) slots are kept at a bootable value before any instance restart — e.g. re-seed each deferred slot to its current value in-window, or use the value-preserving apply (staging current values as value_wo) described in the ticket's own execution comment — so no fail-fast slot is left at CHANGEME.
evidence: Step 1: 'value_wo_version goes absent -> 1 for each migrated slot, so the provider re-sends value_wo = "CHANGEME" once and RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder'
Completion Scope Adjustment: 'rotate ONLY secrets that can be regenerated internally in this session, and flag third-party or externally anchored credentials'

infra/terraform/user_data.sh:294 `if [ "$value" = "CHANGEME" ]; then ... exit 1` over the unconditional PARAMS map (user_data.sh:269-281) which includes gerrit-admin-password, gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key, github-replication-deploy-key, anthropic-api-key
Follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler defers those very slots as externally anchored
findings.finding: The plan carries two mutually inconsistent mechanisms for the migration reset: Step 1 (following the runbook default) resets EVERY migrated SecureString slot to the CHANGEME placeholder on apply, but the Completion Scope Adjustment narrows rotation to only internally self-regenerable secrets and defers the rest to follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler. Several deferred, externally-anchored slots (gerrit-admin-password, gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key, github-replication-deploy-key, anthropic-api-key) are in user_data.sh's UNCONDITIONAL CHANGEME fail-fast map, so if their re-seed is deferred the instance cannot boot after any restart in the gap. The plan never states how deferred slots are kept at a bootable value (e.g. re-seeding the current value, or using the value-preserving apply the ticket comment describes).
scenarios: Migration applied with the CHANGEME reset, deferred externally-anchored slots not re-seeded, instance reboots or a fresh launch occurs -> cloud-init fail-fast exit 1 -> prod box does not come up
Autodeploy timer or ASG replacement fires during the deferral window on a CHANGEME placeholder
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the value-preserving cutover the execution comment already used (stage current live values as value_wo behind a fail-closed var so the forced first send writes byte-identical values), OR require re-seeding every deferred slot to its current value immediately after apply, and state that no instance restart may occur while any fail-fast slot holds CHANGEME.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the contradiction between Step 2 ('rotate the crown-jewels explicitly') and the Completion Scope Adjustment/follow-up (which defers those same crown jewels) by rewriting Step 2 to distinguish internally self-regenerable secrets (rotate now) from externally-anchored crown jewels (flag to auspicial-wily-warbler, do not rotate autonomously).
evidence: Step 2: 'Rotate the crown-jewels explicitly ... Gerrit admin password, opcert Ed25519 signing key, rebar-bot signing key, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys'
Completion Scope Adjustment: 'Externally anchored secrets are tracked in follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler ... intentionally not blockers for this ticket's close'
auspicial-wily-warbler description lists /rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password, opcert-ed25519-key, rebar-bot-signing-key, anthropic-api-key, jira-api-token, gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key as deferred
findings.finding: Step 2 gives a mandatory instruction to rotate the crown-jewel secrets (Gerrit admin password, opcert Ed25519 signing key, rebar-bot signing key, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys) 'explicitly ... they must be treated as compromised', but the later Completion Scope Adjustment and the linked follow-up auspicial-wily-warbler defer exactly those same secrets as externally anchored and 'intentionally not blockers for this ticket's close'. The plan thus contains two contradictory directives for the same secret set, leaving an implementer unsure whether the crown jewels are in-scope to rotate now or deferred.
findings.location: Steps §2 vs Completion Scope Adjustment / Acceptance Criteria line 2
scenarios: Implementer reads Step 2 and rotates the crown jewels (breaking external trust without coordination), contradicting the operator-narrowed scope
Implementer reads the Adjustment and defers everything, contradicting Step 2's 'rotate explicitly'
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite Step 2 to split the secret list into (a) internally self-regenerable slots rotated in this session and (b) externally-anchored/third-party slots that are flagged by name to auspicial-wily-warbler and NOT rotated here, keeping the compromise-treatment language but pointing external rotation at the follow-up ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a resumable/idempotent re-seed procedure: enumerate the exact slot set (18 + 4 rubied MCP-PAT), track per-slot rotation completion in the session artifact, and make step 2 safely re-runnable so an interrupted cutover resumes without double-rotating or missing a slot.
evidence: Step 1: 'RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder'
Step 2: 're-seed/ROTATE every affected secret out-of-band' with no ordering, checklist, or resume-on-interruption handling
ABSENCE: no resumable/idempotent recovery for a rotation interrupted mid-way across the ~18 slots + 4 rubied MCP-PAT params
findings.finding: The migration is not online/expand-contract and offers no per-slot resumability: step 1 resets EVERY migrated secret to the `CHANGEME` placeholder on the first apply, and step 2 re-seeds/rotates them, but the plan does not describe how a partially-completed rotation (apply done, only some slots re-seeded) is resumed or made idempotent. A crash or interruption between apply and full re-seed leaves an unknown subset of crown-jewel secrets stuck on the placeholder with no re-runnable recovery procedure.
scenarios: Operator applies (all slots reset to CHANGEME), rotates 5 of 11 secrets, then the session dies; there is no recorded per-slot progress state to resume from
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-slot checklist artifact (names only) that records rotated/not-rotated state; drive step 2 off it and re-run to completion, treating already-rotated slots as no-ops.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Gate the destructive scrub (step 4) behind a verified-complete rotation of ALL in-scope slots, add a literal DATA LOSS RISK note that the scrub is irreversible, and after deletion assert the surviving tfstate still plans/reads cleanly (post-transformation state check), not merely that versions were deleted.
evidence: Step 4: 'Permanently delete the affected object versions'
Runbook Back-out: 'There is no back-out for the one-time state scrub or the secret rotation: rotated secrets stay rotated.'
ABSENCE: no post-scrub assertion that terraform still plans/reads the surviving state cleanly, and no ordering guarantee that scrub runs strictly AFTER rotation is fully verified
findings.finding: The destructive state-history scrub (step 4) is irreversible and the plan does not assert on the post-failure / post-back-out state. The linked runbook says 'There is no back-out for the one-time state scrub or the secret rotation'; step 4 permanently deletes S3 tfstate object versions. If the apply/rotation is incomplete when the scrub runs — or the scrub itself partially fails — the plan verifies only that live state is clean and that deletion happened, not that state remains internally consistent (e.g. live tfstate still reads/plans cleanly after version deletion, and no not-yet-rotated cleartext survives while a needed history version was destroyed).
findings.location: Step 4 / AC 'Historical cleartext purged...' / runbook §REMEDIATE step 4 and Back-out
scenarios: Scrub deletes versions while a slot was never rotated — a now-retired-but-still-live cleartext value is destroyed from history yet the trust anchor was never updated
delete-object-version corrupts or leaves the backend state unreadable on the next terraform run
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit precondition 'scrub only after step 3 verification passes for every slot' and a post-scrub `terraform plan` sanity check; consider bucket-roll/lifecycle-expire (retire) over hard delete to preserve a recovery path.
